listing.name: Atlantis: The Lost Tales (Atlantis Native)
listing.summary: A native engine for Atlantis: The Lost Tales using your own original game data.

steps.title: Choose your edition of Atlantis
steps.instruction: In Atlantis Native, add your own Atlantis: The Lost Tales edition with matching atlantis.exe and BIGCD1.BIG through BIGCD4.BIG. Keep the complete original folder. Use the upstream edition table for the exact language and build.

steps.title: Start the Linux desktop player
steps.instruction: Extract the matching v0.6.0 Linux tar.gz and open atlantis-native. Both the x86-64 and ARM64 builds need glibc 2.35 or later and ALSA. On Windows 11 ARM, choose the Windows ARM64 ZIP and keep its folder together. Maintain the ARM builds through upstream.

warnings: Preserve the original data and whole effective profile, including games.txt, settings and the edition-specific checkpoint directory. The player shares this profile between copies on the same account.

references.title: Open the matching Mac app
references.instruction: Choose the Intel or Apple silicon v0.6.0 DMG, copy Atlantis Native.app out of it and open it on macOS 11 or later. Keep ~/Library/Application Support/atlantis-native. On Linux the profile normally uses $XDG_DATA_HOME/atlantis-native or ~/.local/share/atlantis-native.

references.title: Set up the PortMaster edition
references.instruction: On a compatible ARM64 PortMaster device, unpack the v0.6.0 PortMaster ZIP into ports and put your original first-game files in ports/atlantisnative/gamedata. Use the firmware menu to launch it. Keep the port folder, its saves directory and any ATLANTIS_SAVES override. This build needs the firmware SDL2 and glibc 2.31 or later.

presentation.manual_preparation: On Play, use the upstream in-process library and original-data picker with your own supported Atlantis: The Lost Tales copy: the edition-matched atlantis.exe and BIGCD1.BIG through BIGCD4.BIG. Keep the complete original tree and supported language/build together; GOG and supported CD editions are alternatives, not interchangeable executables. Upstream can prepare your own discs/images; no game content is downloaded by this engine operation. This offer is Atlantis I only. Normal logs, games.txt, per-build players/checkpoints/settings live under the current account’s AppData/atlantis-native on Windows or XDG data home on Linux; when that location is unavailable the dedicated atlantis-native-data directory is relative to the creating runtime. Core preserves that declared local directory; it does not import or back up the shared external profile or originals. Preserve all actual original/profile roots and the compatible creating engine before changes. Normal start remains in one process; adding a second engine copy does not isolate shared profiles. The Linux x86-64 player requires glibc 2.35 or later and ALSA.
